candidate_relations.reason: The clinical record confirms orbital abscess extending from right-sided rhinosinusitis (matching C001), but the reference diagnosis specifically targets CN7 paresis as the final diagnostic object with acute bacterial sinusitis as its etiology. C001 identifies the anatomical complication (orbital abscess) rather than the cranial nerve deficit that is the requested endpoint. The orbital abscess is a manifestation/component of the same infectious process but does not constitute the complete equivalent of CN7 paresis secondary to acute bacterial sinusitis.
candidate_relations.scope_detail: Orbital abscess secondary to rhinosinusitis is a complication/component of the disease process but does not capture the CN7 paresis, which is the specific neurological endpoint requested by the reference diagnosis.

case_quality_flags: Reference diagnosis focuses on CN7 paresis as the primary endpoint; orbital abscess is a documented complication in the same case but represents a different diagnostic object.
Pathology showed no fungal elements, supporting bacterial etiology consistent with reference diagnosis.
House-Brackmann III right facial paresis explicitly documented, anchoring CN7 paresis as the primary requested diagnosis.
